chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, from his father, who said:
"Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" is closer to the Greatest Name of Allah than the pupil of the eye is to its whiteness.

key_terms.اسْمِ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمِ: The Greatest Name of Allah, denoting the most exalted divine name
key_terms.الرَّحِيمِ: The Especially Merciful, indicating enduring mercy
key_terms.الرَّحْمٰنِ: The All-Merciful, indicating vast universal mercy
key_terms.بَيَاضِهَا: Its whiteness, used in the simile of extreme closeness
key_terms.بِسْمِ: In the name of; the opening invocation beginning with Allah’s name
key_terms.نَاظِرِ الْعَيْنِ: The pupil or sight-center of the eye

ai.seo_question: How close is "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" to the Greatest Name of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith states the immense nearness of the formula "Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm" to the Greatest Name of Allah. It highlights the exalted spiritual rank of the basmalah and its special significance in worship and divine remembrance.
